1.note: Deut 32:36 "וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזוּב", an obscure phrase ("none shut up or left free"). Here it seems to mean that nothing at all was left to give.

2.note: Amos 9:9 "not a pebble (צְרוֹר) falls to the ground". צְרוֹר is also a bundle or purse, as in the "bundles of money" above: not one purse is let go.

3.note: A pun that English cannot keep: זְקֵנִים "elders" and זְקָנִים "beards".

4.note: טוֹטֶפֶת is the word of the tefillin (Exod 13:16), which are not worn on the Sabbath. It is not clear if the joke is his ignorance or only his showy dress.

5.note: The morning blessing "Asher yatsar" says "who formed man in wisdom (בְּחָכְמָה)" (b. Berakhot 60b). He says בְּהֵמָה, "a beast".

6.note: Ps 19:14 "גַּם מִזֵּדִים חֲשֹׂךְ עַבְדֶּךָ" (keep back Your servant from presumptuous sins). He reads מִזֵּדִים as מִזֵּיתִים "from olives" and חֲשֹׂךְ as חֲנֹךְ "train, dedicate". The result has no sense.

7.note: Ps 147:14 "חֵלֶב חִטִּים" (the fat of the wheat). With one letter changed in each word (ל to ר, ט to ד) it becomes "a sword of sharp ones": a blessing turns into a threat.

8.note: Ps 147:8 "בְּעָבִים" (with clouds). He reads בְּגָדִים "clothes"; the words look alike in Hebrew script.

9.note: Ps 149:2 "יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֹשָׂיו" (Israel in his Maker). He says Ishmael and Esau, the usual names for Islam and Christendom: the cantor makes Israel's enemies rejoice.

10.note: Ps 150:4 "בְּמִנִּים וְעוּגָב" (with strings and pipe). He says גְבִינִים "cheeses" and עוּגָה "a cake".

11.note: 1 Chr 29:12, said in the morning service: "לְגַדֵּל וּלְחַזֵּק" (to make great and to strengthen). He says לְגַדֵּף "to blaspheme" and לְהַזִּיק "to do harm". The Hebrew has no "he said" in this line.

12.note: כָּרִים are lambs (Deut 32:14); אֶשְׁכָּר is a gift or tribute (Ps 72:10, Ezek 27:15). The sense is: as precious as the offerings.

13.note: A qerovah (plural qerovot) is a cycle of piyyutim set into the blessings of the Amidah, said by the cantor. The whole debate is on these additions to the fixed prayer.

14.note: A pun: not the songs of the holy ones (קְדוֹשִׁים) but of the קְדֵשִׁים, the cult prostitutes of 1 Kgs 14:24.

15.note: A pun: עִדִּים are the soiled rags of Isa 64:5 ("בֶגֶד עִדִּים"); עֲדָיִים are ornaments.

16.note: A legal term: the prayer leader's prayer discharges the duty of one who cannot pray for himself (m. Rosh Hashanah 4:9). This cantor's prayer does not.

17.note: "The West" (מַעֲרָב) is probably North Africa (the Maghreb). "Greece" (יָוָן) is the Byzantine lands.

18.note: A pun: his prayer (תְּפִלָּה) is folly (תִּפְלָה, as in Job 1:22, Jer 23:13).

19.note: A pun: his praise (תְּהִלָּה) is error (תָּהֳלָה, Job 4:18).

20.note: Deut 18:11 "וְחֹבֵר חָבֶר", one who casts spells, among the forbidden diviners. A pun on his title הֶחָבֵר, "the Ḥaver" (an associate, a scholar). Nothing more is known here about this Benjamin of Arbel.

21.note: Literally "until he threw the jug". The idiom is not clear; the sense from context: his folly stayed hidden until he poured it out in writing.

22.note: Va-yeḥal Moshe (Exod 32:11-14 and 34:1-10) is the Torah reading of fast days. It holds the thirteen attributes, "And the LORD passed before him" (Exod 34:6), which are said in every selihah.

23.note: Literally "called redemption to it": the release of what was held, as of land or a pledge (Lev 25:24). The folly shut up in his heart went free when he spoke.

24.note: A turn of Prov 16:26 "נֶפֶשׁ עָמֵל עָמְלָה לּוֹ" (the worker's soul toils for itself): his toil helps only others. The reading of "his opponents" (מְרִיבָיו) in the first half is uncertain.

25.note: "His due" (גְּמוּלָה) can be reward or punishment. The next lines show punishment, so "this" is probably the qerovah: whoever calls it a duty.
